Code 57/1/1, SET~1, BIOLOGY (Theory), 3 hours, 70 marks, 31 printed pages, 33 questions); idx 1 is the Hindi instructions plus the Hindi Q1; every ODD index 1-29 is the Hindi facing page. The contact sheet, the text layer of every odd page and full-size reads of every even page show no English overflow onto an odd page, no parity inversion, and an English final page (idx 30, Q33(b)). Born-digital paper: the text layer was a DRAFT only and every row was checked on the full-size page (the layer drops the quoted labels, the sigma/rho symbols, the en dashes in Q22 and Q33(b), the half-mark fractions and whole stem fragments). Instruction (viii) prints the count: 1 internal choice in Section B, 1 in C, 2 in D, 3 in E = seven alternatives (Q19, Q28, Q29(d), Q30(b), Q31, Q32, Q33), each confirmed against a bare OR in the marking scheme and on the page. Q29's printed sub-part marks are 1, 1/2, 1/2, 2 (the scheme agrees), so Q29b and Q29c carry 0.5. Primary marks: A16 + B10 + C21 + D8 + E15 = 70. Section-A key read on the scheme IMAGE and from the scheme's text layer, 16 of 16 agreeing: BCAADCCCACBDCACA, Q7 printed as a dual key (c) // (d). Quotes straight, scientific names plain text (the Biology rules). The assertion-reason context and options are byte-identical to the pilot 2024-57-1-1 (same printed wording).

questions.stem: The graph plotted below is based on the data collected by biology students with respect to the levels of oxygen at the specific points in the river flowing outside their city. Which point in the graph indicates the entry of untreated sewage in the river ?
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a graph of Level against Distance along River with two curves, Dissolved oxygen (solid) and Mineral ions (dashed), and four vertical lines marked (i) to (iv); how the two curves behave at each line is the whole question, so it is withheld here. Page idx 6.
questions._flag: TWO NOTES. (1) Key: CBSE keys (a) Point (i), where dissolved oxygen is lowest and mineral ions highest. A dynamic reading of the same graph could argue for (iv), where dissolved oxygen starts to fall and mineral ions start to rise downstream; the official key is kept and the solution teaches the scheme's reading. (2) Chapter: this is water pollution by sewage (the old NCERT Environmental Issues chapter, not on this exam's axis); filed on the closest live subtopic, Microbes in Sewage Treatment, which teaches BOD and why untreated sewage depletes oxygen.

questions._cbseVoided: The scheme prints two complete answer sets separated by '//': "(a) Recessive trait, both the parents in generation I do not express the trait yet it appears in the progeny. (b) Autosomal trait, both male and females have equal chances of getting the trait. (c) Child '1' : Aa/AA , Child '3' : Aa // (a) Recessive trait, both the parents in generation I do not express the trait, yet it appears in the progeny. (b) Sex linked trait, comparatively more male are getting affected. (c) Child '1' : XY, Child '3' : X' X(carrier)"

questions._flag: EITHER OF TWO ANSWERS ACCEPTED: the scheme credits both an autosomal-recessive and a sex-linked-recessive reading of the pedigree, with matching genotypes. The solution gives both and says which the chart supports.

| (2) | Natural, passive | No | 'R' | Across the placenta during pregnancy/breast feeding |
| (3) | Acquired, active | 'S' | Yes | Getting a vaccine during breast feeding |
| (4) | Acquired, passive | 'T' | No | Getting an injection of antibodies |
